entry.title: Abortion is on the ballot again as post-Roe policies continue to evolve
entry.summary: Four states will vote on abortion-related ballot measures in November. The measures follow the Supreme Court's "Dobbs" decision, which upended federal abortion protections.

entry.title: Your smartwatch isn't accurately counting how many calories you burn, study says
entry.summary: A new study finds that consumer-grade fitness wearables are generally inaccurate when calculating calories burned. NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with the study's lead author Jason Kostrna.

entry.title: Is produce from a home garden safer than store bought? 'It depends'
entry.summary: A record-breaking summer for foodborne illness prompted more consumers to grow produce at home. But experts say it's the farming practices, not size, that matters for food safety.

entry.title: These stunning photos capture the hard yet fulfilling lives of fisherfolk
entry.summary: In the bustling heart of the southern Indian city of Chennai is a market that never sleeps, where residents from the poorest neighborhoods wage a battle of survival with the sea.

entry.title: Betel nuts are a top mind-affecting substance. Now there's evidence of ancient use
entry.summary: New research on ancient human remains suggests the habitual usage of betel nuts, a plant seed with mind-affecting properties that is popular in parts of Asia despite the health risks it presents.

entry.title: Will even one of the U.N.'s 17 'sustainable development goals' be met by 2030?
entry.summary: The 17 goals agreed upon by world leaders are incredibly ambitious. Are we even close to achieving any of them? If we don't, is the project a failure?

entry.title: Doctors raise concerns about views and experience of members on federal task force
entry.summary: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. names new members to powerful federal task force that plays a key role in determining the kind of preventive case people get. In a major departure, the new members of the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force include specialists instead of experts on preventive care and general medicine, raising fears among many doctors.

entry.title: To prevent deaths in childbirth, Kenyan moms turn to an AI powered chatbot
entry.summary: Many questions come up during pregnancy. Is swelling normal? Are avocados safe to eat? For folks in Kenya who don't have a search engine at their fingertips, a chatbot is offering a lifeline.

entry.title: A year ago, President Trump pledged to lower Medicaid drug prices. Has that happened?
entry.summary: The Trump administration's efforts to lower drug prices included promised changes to Medicaid. But it's still unclear which drugs will be affected. And each state has to opt in.

entry.title: Trump's surgeon general pick faces questions on vaccines and vaping at Senate hearing
entry.summary: The Senate committee on health held a confirmation hearing for three top health officials, including surgeon general. Dr. Nicole Saphier is President Trump's third pick to be the nation's top doctor.
